analysis.title: Airbnb Inc. (ABNB) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Strong Execution Across Core Initiatives Drives Raised FY26 Expectations
key_insights: GS reiterates Neutral on ABNB and raises the 12-month price target to $185 from $165. Price was $170.13 at the 5 Nov 2026 close, implying 8.7% upside.
Q3'26 beat GS and consensus on gross bookings, revenue and Adj. EBITDA. GS describes it as the fastest revenue growth in over three years.

Nights & Seats Booked grew +16% YoY and GBV grew +21% YoY. All five core markets (US, France, UK, Canada, Australia) improved, and nights booked from most expansion markets accelerated alongside core markets.
Management raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to high-teens % YoY from mid-teens. FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin guidance rose to at least 36% from at least 35.5%.

AI is now resolving about 40% of customer support issues without human agents. Support cost per booking fell more than 17% YoY. ABNB shipped 50+ products/features in Q3 (+70% YoY). A dedicated AI travel agent is planned for 1H27.
ABNB is expanding beyond accommodations into hotels, services, car rentals, experiences and partnerships, including a new American Express partnership that expands distribution to Amex Travel.
Capital return: $700m of buybacks in Q3, $2.7bn left on the existing authorization, and a new $12bn Class A repurchase authorization.

Negatives: Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA margin is guided down slightly vs Q4'25 on marketing timing and reinvestment. Cancellation rates rose to 19% from 16% a year ago. Q3 take rate came in modestly below GS and Street expectations because the RNPL expansion delays booking revenue recognition and booking options are more flexible.

GS raised FY26 estimates: revenue $14,409m (from $14,165m), Adj. EBITDA $5,194m (from $5,056m), GAAP EPS $5.54 (from $5.41). FY27 revenue rose to $16,062m (from $15,714m) and GAAP EPS fell to $6.32 (from $6.51).

The PT rests on an equal blend of 22.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA (from 20.0x) on NTM+1 year estimates and 20.0x EV/FCF-SBC (from 18.0x) on NTM+4 year estimates discounted 3 years at 12%. GS raised both multiples to reflect higher estimates on operating momentum.
GS expects investor focus on whether the demand acceleration and first-time booker trends persist into 2027, and on how well ABNB monetizes hotels, services, experiences and partnerships.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral reiterated and PT raised to $185 from $165 after a beat and raised FY26 guidance. GS raised its valuation multiples on higher estimates and operating momentum.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (GAAP unless noted) vs GS est / consensus: gross bookings $27,719m vs $26,164m / $26,300m. Revenue $4,869m vs $4,721m / $4,749m. Adj. EBITDA $2,509m vs $2,347m / $2,364m. GAAP EPS $3.16 vs $2.89 / $2.85.
Q3'26 reported nights/experiences booked 155.0m vs GS 148.3m / consensus 148.5m. GBV per night $179 vs $176 / $177. Take rate 17.6% vs 18.0% / 18.1%. Adj. EBITDA margin 51.5% vs 49.7% / 49.8%.
FY26 guidance: revenue growth high-teens % YoY (prior mid-teens) and Adj. EBITDA margin of at least 36% (prior at least 35.5%). Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA margin guided down slightly vs Q4'25.

GS Q4'26 estimates (new vs old): GBV $23.57bn vs $22.96bn, revenue $3.25bn vs $3.16bn, GAAP EPS $0.77 vs $0.90. The report text gives Q4 Adj. EBITDA as '$905bn' (from '$926bn'), which Exhibit 2 shows as $905m (from $926m).
GS FY27 estimates (new vs old): GBV $119.28bn vs $116.73bn, revenue $16.06bn vs $15.71bn, Adj. EBITDA $5.97bn vs $5.82bn, GAAP EPS $6.32 vs $6.51. FY28 GAAP EPS $7.14 vs $7.57 old.
Cancellation rate was 19% vs 16% a year ago.
risk_factors: Faster or slower growth in overall travel demand, and the pace of adoption of alternative accommodations as a travel category.
Success in gaining market share in international markets.
Competitive intensity across the online travel funnel.
Whether new categories on the platform are adopted by existing and new users.
Investments in new products and geographies may take faster or slower to show up in growth.
Rising cancellation rates and a lower take rate from RNPL expansion and more flexible booking options.
